cards.name: Liquify
cards.summary: Opens the Liquify workspace, where brush tools push, pull, twirl, pucker and bloat pixels as if the image were a thick fluid (Forward Warp, Reconstruct, Smooth, Twirl, Pucker, Bloat, Push Left, Freeze / Thaw Mask) and Face-Aware sliders reshape eyes, nose, mouth and face outline on detected faces. The result is smoothly reshaped or smeared pixels; the warp itself is made by hand in the dialog, the harvest found no keys that describe it.
use_for: subtle body or face reshaping in portrait and fashion retouching
caricature, melting or bulging distortion for a poster or meme visual
bending a logo or texture so it follows the folds of fabric or a curved product
liquid, smeared abstract backgrounds from a colourful photo
avoid: unattended scripts: there are no harvested params for the strokes (declared_params 0), so an empty DialogModes.NO call has nothing to apply; a person has to warp in the dialog (Save Mesh / Load Mesh reuse a warp)
straight lines near the warp (flag poles, podium edges, door frames) bend visibly: paint a Freeze Mask over them first
heavy face reshaping of real people in news or documentary images misrepresents them
vector artwork or type that must stay editable: rasterise first or convert to a smart object; for a controlled pin- or grid-based bend use Edit/Puppet Warp or Edit/Transform/Warp instead
cards.scripting: executeAction(charIDToTypeID("LqFy"), undefined, DialogModes.ALL); // no stringID is registered for LqFy (harvest); no keys describe the strokes, so DialogModes.NO with an empty descriptor (it runs, 1146 ms in the harvest) has no warp to apply: the dialog route needs a person
cards.cost: medium: 1146 ms just to run on the 480x270 harvest layer; the real cost is the manual brush work, and large files make the brushes lag

review.changes: Puppet Warp is not a numeric bend: reworded that alternative; rest checked (shortcut, LqFy charID, smart_filter true, 1146 ms, declared_params 0; AI Warp tool and CDR Smudge point back to Liquify)

verified.note: Untested: no frame: the warp is brushed by hand in the Liquify workspace; no harvested keys describe it (status needs_input).

second_opinion.note: Checked: id absent from gallery/ps_filter/index.json, listed in gallery/ps_filter/not_rendered.json; a harness limit (no scripted route or required input), not a filter fault; status 'needs_input' kept.

cards.name: Neural Filters
cards.summary: Opens the Neural Filters workspace, a gallery of machine-learning filters (portrait retouching such as Skin Smoothing and Smart Portrait, Style Transfer, Colorize, Photo Restoration, Depth Blur, Super Zoom, Harmonization and others) that each have their own sliders; models download on first use and some filters run in Adobe's cloud. Which filters this 27.4 install offers was not harvested, and the harvest did not run it.
use_for: one-click skin smoothing or JPEG artefact clean-up on a portrait
colourising or restoring an old black-and-white photo
matching the colour and light of a pasted element to its background (Harmonization)
turning a photo into a painted look with Style Transfer
avoid: unattended scripts: it opens its own workspace and downloads or calls cloud models (harvest error); NF_UI_DATA is an opaque object that was not decoded, so a call cannot be built from a spec
offline machines or confidential client images: cloud filters need sign-in and upload the image
changing the expression, age or gaze of real people in news images (Smart Portrait) misrepresents them
precise, repeatable results: the models can change between versions; use classic filters or Camera Raw for reproducible looks

params.name: NF_UI_DATA
params.does: Data: the chosen filters and their slider values as one opaque object (not decoded by the harvest)
params.typical: recorded from the workspace, never written by hand

params.name: NF_OUTPUT_TYPE
params.does: Output Type: where the result goes (the workspace's Output menu: current layer, new layer, smart filter, new document ...); the integer codes were not harvested
params.typical: unknown codes: pick the output in the workspace

cards.scripting: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("neuralGalleryFilters"), undefined, DialogModes.ALL); // should open the workspace for a person (the harvest did not run it); keys NF_UI_DATA (object) and NF_OUTPUT_TYPE (integer) are declared in the terminology but were never run or decoded, so no DialogModes.NO call can be built
cards.non_destructive: only when the workspace's output is set to a smart filter or a new layer; the harvest did not test it
cards.cost: heavy: model downloads on first use, GPU work or a cloud round trip per filter; not timed (not executed)

review.changes: scripting comment no longer states as fact that the DialogModes.ALL call opens the workspace (never run); rest checked against the declared keys and the harvest error

verified.note: Untested: no frame: each neural filter is set in its own workspace with downloaded models (status needs_input).

cards.name: Vanishing Point
cards.summary: Opens the Vanishing Point dialog, where you click four corners to define perspective planes (blue grid = valid plane), tear off connected planes around corners, then clone, paint or paste artwork onto them; pasted art is scaled and skewed to the plane so it sits on the wall, floor or box side in correct perspective. Planes and pasted content come from the dialog and the clipboard, not from harvested keys.
use_for: placing a poster, logo or signage design onto a photographed wall, billboard or shop front
packaging mockups: wrapping artwork around two or three sides of a box
removing objects from tiled floors, windows or brick walls by cloning in perspective
extending a building facade or floor pattern in perspective
avoid: unattended scripts: no keys describe the planes or the pasted art, so an empty DialogModes.NO call (it runs, 297 ms in the harvest) has nothing to place
CMYK, Grayscale or Lab documents: the harvest lists RGB only; convert to RGB first
smart objects: not available as a smart filter (harvest: command not currently available); add an empty layer and work on that so the result stays separate
curved surfaces such as bottles or flags: use Edit/Puppet Warp or Edit/Transform/Warp; for an editable flat placement use Edit/Transform/Perspective on a smart object
cards.scripting: executeAction(charIDToTypeID("VnPt"), undefined, DialogModes.ALL); // no stringID is registered for VnPt (harvest); copy the artwork to the clipboard first, then draw planes and paste in the dialog: a person is needed
cards.cost: light to run (297 ms with an empty descriptor on the 480x270 harvest layer); the time goes into drawing planes by hand

review.changes: none (RGB-only modes, smart-filter error, 297 ms, Ctrl+Alt+V and VnPt charID match the batch; AI Perspective Grid and CDR Draw in Perspective exist)

verified.note: Untested: no frame: needs perspective planes drawn in its dialog and pasted art (status needs_input).

second_opinion.note: Checked: id absent from gallery/ps_filter/index.json, listed in gallery/ps_filter/not_rendered.json; a harness limit (no scripted route or required input), not a filter fault; status 'needs_input' kept.

cards.name: Add Noise
cards.summary: Scatters random pixel values over the image like sensor noise or film grain. Gaussian distribution gives a speckled, stronger grain than Uniform at the same Percent; Monochromatic adds only grey (luminance) grain instead of red, green and blue specks.
use_for: grain to stop banding in gradients and flat AI-generated skies before print or video export
matching the grain of a pasted cut-out or clean graphic to a noisy photo
gritty, analogue texture for a poster, album cover or risograph look
added to a 50% grey layer set to Overlay, as adjustable grain over the whole design
avoid: low-resolution web images: noise makes JPEG files bigger and blockier
high Percent with colour (non-monochromatic) noise looks like cheap sensor noise; keep it monochromatic for film grain
small type and hairlines: speckles break thin strokes, so apply grain under the type layer
a non-destructive, editable grain: Layer/New Adjustment Layer/Grain or Filter/Camera Raw Filter grain

params.name: noise
params.does: Percent: how strong the noise is
params.typical: 2-6 for subtle grain or dithering; 15-30 for a gritty look

params.name: distort
params.does: Distribution: Uniform spreads values evenly; Gaussian gives more speckled, stronger grain

params.name: monochromatic
params.does: only lightness noise (grey grain) instead of coloured specks
params.typical: true for film grain, false for digital noise

pairs_with: Overlay blend mode on a 50% grey layer
cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(s("noise"), charIDToTypeID("#Prc"), 25); d.putEnumerated(s("distort"), s("distort"), s("gaussianDistribution")); d.putBoolean(s("monochromatic"), false); executeAction(s("addNoise"), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the last-used values; the harvest could not read a Percent range; the result descriptor reported 12.5 / uniform for the gallery's 25 / gaussian run, but the frame's noise (std about 55 levels, 57 % of pixels off by more than 32) is beyond what uniform 12.5 % can make, so the sent values were applied
cards.non_destructive: yes as a smart filter on a smart object: the harvest applied it to a smart object and read the filterFX entry back, storing distort, monochromatic and noise (harvest/ps/ps_filter.json extra.smart_filter, probed after this batch was cut); on a plain pixel layer it rewrites the pixels
cards.cost: light: 67 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer

review.changes: non_destructive now cites the harvest's smart-filter probe instead of 'this harvest did not test it'; keys, enum, #Prc unit and demo checked

verified.note: Strong RGB colour specks over the whole frame (1:1 crop: noise std about 55 levels, 57 % of pixels off by more than 32), more than Uniform 12.5 % could give (it stops at +/-32), so the frame used the Gaussian 25 % sent and the read-back (12.5 / uniform) is stale like the other 11.

cards.name: Despeckle
cards.summary: One-step noise removal with no settings: it finds edges (areas of strong colour change) and blurs everything except those edges, so fine speckle and grain soften while outlines stay. The change is subtle; it is often run two or three times.
use_for: quick clean-up of grainy scans or phone photos before printing
softening halftone dots or JPEG speckle in a scanned logo or document
a first pass before sharpening a noisy image
avoid: already soft images such as video frames: there is little to remove and the change is barely visible
strong or coloured noise: use Filter/Noise/Reduce Noise or Filter/AI Denoise, which have controls
repeated passes on faces: skin turns waxy and fine texture disappears
1-px lines and fine hairlines: Despeckle treats them as speckle (a 1 px white hairline on the plate dropped from 255 to 118 while 2 px and wider lines stayed)
cards.non_destructive: yes as a smart filter on a smart object: the harvest applied it to a smart object and read the filterFX entry back, with no stored settings (harvest/ps/ps_filter.json extra.smart_filter, probed after this batch was cut); on a plain pixel layer it rewrites the pixels
cards.cost: light: 69 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer

review.changes: non_destructive now cites the harvest's smart-filter probe instead of 'this harvest did not test it'

verified.note: Subtle as the card says: on the 1:1 crop the 1-px hairline is knocked down (255 to 118) and the photo softens by under 1 level while 2-px and wider lines and the block edges stay untouched (max 5 levels); the plate has no grain, so the noise-removal claim itself rests on that thin-line behaviour.

cards.name: Dust & Scratches
cards.summary: Finds pixels that differ from their neighbours by more than Threshold and replaces them with the median of the pixels within Radius, which removes dust spots and thin scratches. At a larger Radius or a low Threshold the whole image turns into soft, blotchy, painterly patches and thin lines and small type disappear.
use_for: removing dust and scratches from scanned photos and film
cleaning sensor dust spots in a flat sky (inside a selection)
smoothing skin or backgrounds as a base for frequency-separation retouching
a blotchy, watercolour-like texture at high Radius
avoid: the whole image at high Radius: detail, type and edges melt; select the damaged area first and keep Radius as small as removes the spots
Threshold 0 on a photo you want to keep sharp: every pixel is replaced, which is the same as a strong Median
single large blemishes: the Spot Healing Brush or Content-Aware Fill gives cleaner results
scripts that rely on exact values: the harvest read-back echoed the stored values whatever was sent, so check the pixels after a scripted run

params.name: radius
params.does: Radius: how far, in pixels, it looks for replacement values; bigger removes larger spots but blurs more
params.typical: 1-4 for dust on scans; 8-20 for a painterly look

params.name: threshold
params.does: Threshold: how far, in brightness levels, a pixel must differ before it is replaced; higher keeps more texture
params.typical: raise from 0 until grain returns while the spots stay gone (often 10-40)

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("radius"), 10); d.putInteger(s("threshold"), 0); executeAction(s("dustAndScratches"), d, DialogModes.NO); // an empty descriptor runs with the stored values (harvest audit); sent values are honoured (gallery: the values sent reproduce the frame, the reported 16 / 20 do not); the result descriptor reports the last-used values
cards.non_destructive: yes as a smart filter on a smart object: the harvest applied it to a smart object and read the filterFX entry back, storing radius and threshold (harvest/ps/ps_filter.json extra.smart_filter, probed after this batch was cut); on a plain pixel layer it rewrites the pixels
cards.cost: light at small Radius; grows with Radius on large images (not timed by the harvest)

review.changes: removed the invented 0-255 Threshold range (the harvest read no range); non_destructive now cites the harvest's smart-filter probe instead of 'this harvest did not test it'

verified.note: Threshold 0 turns the whole frame into soft blotchy patches: the type becomes blobs, the hairlines merge, block corners round off; the stale read-back (16 / 20) is not what was applied.

cards.name: Median
cards.summary: Replaces every pixel with the median brightness of the pixels within Radius. Noise and specks vanish and texture flattens into smooth patches with rounded corners; at larger Radius the image looks like a blobby watercolour or posterised painting and thin lines and small type are wiped out.
use_for: removing salt-and-pepper noise or halftone dots from a scan
smoothing a jagged layer mask or selection edge
a soft, blobby painterly background behind a headline
simplifying a photo into flat shapes before Image Trace or posterising
avoid: images with type, hairlines or fine detail you want to keep: anything thinner than about the Radius disappears
faces at high Radius: features turn plastic; mask them out
plain blur with soft edges: use Filter/Blur/Gaussian Blur; for edge-preserving smoothing use Filter/Blur/Surface Blur

params.name: radius
params.does: Radius: the neighbourhood size in pixels; bigger = flatter, blobbier result
params.typical: 1-3 for noise; 8-25 for a painterly look; 2-10 on masks

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(s("radius"), charIDToTypeID("#Pxl"), 15); executeAction(s("median"), d, DialogModes.NO); // radius 1-500 (harvest clamp); the smart-filter record stores radius as a pixel unit double; the terminology declares an integer, so d.putInteger(s("radius"), 15) is the alternative if the unit form is refused
cards.non_destructive: yes as a smart filter on a smart object: the harvest applied it to a smart object and read the filterFX entry back, storing radius (harvest/ps/ps_filter.json extra.smart_filter, probed after this batch was cut); on a plain pixel layer it rewrites the pixels
cards.cost: light: 163 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; slower at large Radius

review.changes: non_destructive now cites the harvest's smart-filter probe instead of 'this harvest did not test it'; scripting notes the pixel-unit form the smart filter stores

verified.note: Texture flattens into smooth patches with rounded block corners, the type is wiped to specks and the hairlines merge into one bar, the blobby median look described.

cards.name: Reduce Noise
cards.summary: Classic noise-reduction dialog: Strength and Preserve Details smooth luminance noise, Reduce Color Noise removes coloured blotches, Sharpen Details restores some edge crispness and Remove JPEG Artifact softens JPEG compression blocks. The result is a cleaner, smoother image that turns waxy when pushed.
use_for: cleaning low-light or high-ISO photos before print
removing colour blotches and JPEG blocks from a compressed video frame or web image
preparing a noisy photo for upscaling or for a large poster background
avoid: calling it with an empty descriptor: Photoshop refuses it (program error, harvest); send colorNoise, sharpen and removeJPEGArtifact, the descriptor the harvest ran (channelDenoise was not sent, so it is optional)
high Strength on faces: skin goes plastic; keep Preserve Details up or mask faces
images that are already soft, such as the test frame: the visible change is small
best-quality denoising: Filter/AI Denoise or Filter/Camera Raw Filter give cleaner results on photos

hard-edged colour graphics (logos, colour bars, UI): Reduce Color Noise at 100 % bled colour a few pixels across the plate's sharp colour-block borders (blue into violet, magenta into grey); lower it or mask such areas

params.name: colorNoise
params.does: Reduce Color Noise %: removes red / green / blue blotches
params.typical: the result descriptor always reports 45 (the dialog's last-used value), not what was applied; 50-100 on blotchy frames

params.name: sharpen
params.does: Sharpen Details %: puts back some edge contrast lost to smoothing
params.typical: the result descriptor always reports 25 (the dialog's last-used value), not what was applied; 0 for the smoothest result

params.name: removeJPEGArtifact
params.does: Remove JPEG Artifact: softens JPEG compression blocks and ringing
params.typical: true for web or video images

params.name: channelDenoise
params.does: With: list of per-channel settings; the read-back entry holds amount (Strength, read back 6) and edgeFidelity (Preserve Details %, read back 60), its channel reference read back only as <reference>

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s("colorNoise"), 100); d.putInteger(s("sharpen"), 0); d.putBoolean(s("removeJPEGArtifact"), true); executeAction(s("denoise"), d, DialogModes.NO); // an empty descriptor is refused; these three keys (integers / boolean) are the descriptor the harvest ran. The result descriptor executeAction returns is not a read-back for this filter: it reports the dialog's last-used values (proven in the PS effect gallery: re-applying the reported values gives different pixels, the values sent reproduce the frame exactly), so judge a scripted run by its pixels. Strength and Preserve Details stay at the stored values unless you also send the channelDenoise list, untested: var r = new ActionReference(); r.putEnumerated(s("channel"), s("channel"), s("composite")); var c = new ActionDescriptor(); c.putReference(s("channel"), r); c.putInteger(s("amount"), 10); c.putInteger(s("edgeFidelity"), 40); var l = new ActionList(); l.putObject(s("channelDenoiseParams"), c); d.putList(s("channelDenoise"), l); (the composite reference is an assumption: the harvest read it back only as <reference>)
cards.non_destructive: yes as a smart filter on a smart object: the harvest applied it to a smart object and read the filterFX entry back, storing colorNoise, removeJPEGArtifact and sharpen (harvest/ps/ps_filter.json extra.smart_filter, probed after this batch was cut); on a plain pixel layer it rewrites the pixels
cards.cost: medium: 789 ms on the 480x270 harvest test layer; longer on a full-HD frame (not timed)

review.changes: the batch shows the harvest ran it with only colorNoise, sharpen and removeJPEGArtifact (value_sent_for_probe), so 'send every key, including channelDenoise' was wrong: scripting is now that proven three-key call with channelDenoise as an optional, untested add-on; 45 / 25 are no longer called defaults (batch: no defaults recorded, read-back ignores sent values); removed the unsourced 8x8 block size, the composite-channel claim in params and the 'a few seconds on full HD' extrapolation; non_destructive now cites the harvest's smart-filter probe

verified.note: Untested: the soft, noise-free photo plate gives Reduce Noise nothing to clean, so the cleaner / waxy result cannot be judged; the frame only shows Reduce Color Noise 100 % bleeding colour across the strip's hard block borders (blue into violet, magenta into the ramp) on the 1:1 crop, now a card fact. Needs a plate with added luminance + colour noise (or JPEG blocks); the demo settings are not the cause.

previous.note: 960 frame unchanged by eye; on the 1:1 crop the only change is colour bleeding across the hard block borders (blue into violet, magenta into the ramp) and a slight softening: the soft, noise-free plate gives Reduce Noise nothing to clean, so the cleaner / waxy claim cannot be judged here.

second_opinion.note: Overturned weak -> not_rendered (Untested). Re-opened frame + crop: photo unchanged, colour bleed at block borders only. Plate check: no noise or JPEG blocks anywhere on the plate, so raising settings cannot show the effect (and Strength / Preserve Details sit in channelDenoise, not in the demo); this is a plate limit, not a filter fault. Harness check: the result descriptor is stale for this filter, but the frame differs from the plate (crop diff 3.8), so the values sent were applied.
